newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy says Euro likely to be stable, strong.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy says Euro likely to be stable, strong.

text.p: European Monetary Institute President (EMI) Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Friday the Euro was likely to be a "stable, reasonably strong currency" given the future European central bank's (ECB) commitment to stability-oriented monetary policy and other factors.
Lamfalussy told a news conference the Euro would benefit from the rapid development of a Euro-denominated bond market which would become an alternative to investment in dollar paper.
"That can have a bearing on the strength of the Euro," Lamfalussy said. He added that the Euro may also become an invoicing currency.
Lamfalussy said the Euro may become a general reserve currency, establishing a "better balance between the dollar and the Euro area."
"Given the stability-oriented domestic policy and natural changes...the Euro is likely to be a stable, reasonably strong currency," Lamfalussy said.
